ENTRIES CLOSING DATE, MIDNIGHT, AUGUST 17, 1956
NOVICE DRIVERS Must Pass Test Before Qualifying Trials
CARS ELIGIBLE-—Entries will be restricted to 1954, 55 and 56 Models of American Manufacture.
Any hardtop model is eligible, except Commercial Cars, Jeeps and Station Wagons.

STARTING FIELD —The right is reserved by the USAC Officials and Management to increase the
field of starters at their discretion. The fastest thirty (30) qualified cars will be selected first for the
starting field.
If more than 30 cars are permitted to start (limit 40 cars), those cars finishing below 30th position will
receive $2o.00 each. This money will be deducted from the total purse.

HISTORY OF AUTO RACING AT
WISCONSIN STATE FAIR PARK
There's no doubt about it. Auto racing has come a
long way here at Wisconsin State Fair park since Sept. II,
1903 when the first competitive was held on the one
mile oval. William Jones wheeled his Columbia to victory
in a five mile touring car race, beating three other entries,
averaging 35.93 miles per hour. Compare this to Pat
Flaherty's 100 mile mark of 98.96 miles per hour set last
June, and you can see that auto racing has progressed
as much as the auto industry, and has for the most part,
provided and tested many of the mechanical innovations
found on today's high speed pleasure cars.
The fair park one mile track was hewn out of part of a
pasture that old-timers knew as the Ernest Weber farm.

some years earlier. The popularity of horse-racing at the
